text: A Roman feast. Then off to the vomitorium.
Nope. Wrong room entirely.
Romans: the vomitorium myth.
The story says Romans had a room for throwing up.
So they could eat even more.
But a vomitorium was a corridor.
In an amphitheatre or a stadium.
The word means a place that spews out.
It spewed out crowds, not dinner.
The Colosseum had dozens of them.
Tens of thousands could leave in minutes.
Modern stadiums still use them.
So where did the myth come from?
The word sounds like vomit. That's about it.
Writers in the 1900s ran with it.
Did some Romans overeat and throw up? A few, apparently.
But there was no special room.
Rooms just for throwing up: zero.
Crowd exits: lots.
Anyway, here's a Roman heading to the vomitorium.
